characterization_methods.key_findings: γ austenite, α ferrite (increasing with Al), ε martensite (small, low Al), and κ carbide (only at 600 °C for the highest-Al alloy); increasing ferrite content is more relevant to the mechanical trend than κ-carbide or ε-martensite.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm
characterization_methods.purpose: phase identification for the Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl screening series

characterization_methods.key_findings: For Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl (500 °C/24 h): YS and UTS increase with Al (YS to ~690 MPa, UTS to ~900 MPa at ~10.5 wt.% Al) while tensile elongation drops.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; averages of three measurements per material state
characterization_methods.purpose: mechanical screening (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, total elongation)

characterization_methods.key_findings: Hardness minimum ~120–140 HBW near 2 wt.% Al, reaching ~290 HBW at ~10.5 wt.% Al (500 °C/24 h series).

No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in final materials; as-cast samples had coarse dendritic microstructure; hot rolling + water quenching gave fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 μm grain size and retained Mn microsegregations.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction
characterization_methods.purpose: microstructure inspection (cracks, pores, macrosegregations; grain size)
characterization_methods.technique: metallographic analysis (grinding and polishing with standard metallographic techniques)

interfaces.phase_evolution: κ-carbide is not detected at 500 °C/24 h for the Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl series; it appears only after 600 °C aging for the highest-Al alloy. The mechanical trend is attributed mainly to increasing α ferrite content rather than κ-carbide or ε-martensite.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five alloys per system cast stepwise into five movable Cu molds from a 4-kg ingot; Al charged through an air lock to adjust the remaining melt composition.
10×50×130 mm³ blocks hot rolled at 1100 °C into 2±0.1 mm thick, ~500 mm long sheets.
Cut into nine segments of 2×60×55 mm³ per alloy composition.
Homogenization at 1100 °C for 2 h under Ar, followed by water quenching; this is the parent process of the 500 °C/24 h aging step.
Scales removed from surfaces after heat treatments.
Samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation prepared from the segments by package spark erosion.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl series aged 500 °C/24 h (green series in Fig. 6a), plotted versus Al content (data points near 0, 2, 5, 8, ~10.5 wt.%); tensile values are averages of three measurements per material state.

hardness.value: ~290 HBW (500 °C/24 h series at ~10.5 wt.% Al)

elongation.value: ~12–25% at ~10.5 wt.% Al (collapse at high Al; not uniquely attributed to 500 °C/24 h in Fig. 6a)

ultimate_tensile_strength.value: ~900 MPa (500 °C/24 h series at ~10.5 wt.% Al)
~810–840 MPa at 0 wt.% Al (tempered series starting level, including 500 °C/24 h)

yield_strength.value: ~690 MPa (500 °C/24 h series at ~10.5 wt.% Al)
~350 MPa at 0 wt.% Al (starting level of the series; condition not uniquely attributed in Fig. 6a)

phases_present.volume_fraction: ~100 vol.% at 2 wt.% Al; dominant matrix phase

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized microstructure after hot rolling and water quenching (grain size ~20 μm, some retained Mn microsegregations). After aging at 500 °C/24 h, the Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl series shows austenite with increasing α ferrite content as Al increases; κ-carbide is not detected at 500 °C (it appears only at 600 °C for the highest-Al alloy), and a small amount of ε martensite appears at low Al.

unmapped_findings: This sample belongs to the Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl RAP screening group (second alloy class) in which Al content varies between 2 and 11 wt.%; individual Al levels are not enumerated in the text, and Fig. 6 data points are near 0, 2, 5, 8 and ~10.5 wt.% Al (blocks b0019, b0026, figure_006).
